In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VisP is a virulence and stress regulator protein.
VisP is a periplasm protein that interacts with peptidoglycerol and LpxO to regulate LPS modifications and pathogenicity of Gram-negative pathogens.
VisP controls LpxO-dependent and LpxO-independent lipid-A modifications, which have a major impact on bacterial virulence and stress responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VisP controls the lipid-A composition in S. Typhmuriurn, which is essential for virulence.
the periplasmic chaperone protein VisP acts as a regulator of the bacterial cell wall homevostasis, and its role is essential for bacterial virulence.
the VisP-Lpxo interaction is a mechanism to control lipid-A modifications and bacterial cell wall home-ostasis in response to the vacuole intracellular environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VisP and LoxP act independently to control S. Typhmuriurn pathogenicity.

VisP acts through the lipid-A-modifying enzyme LpxO, which is conserved in several pathogens, and thus VisP-LpxOMediated lipid-A modifications may have a broader impact in Gram-negative bacterial pathogenesis.
